messages:
nina: quick sync: riffing on SDK pagination + retries — goal is a single "continuable iteration" mental model but with transport-declared capabilities so we can choose safer defaults.
omar: sounds good. can you enumerate the capabilities you have in mind?
nina: basic set: ["progressive_stream", "server_cursor", "stateless_resume", "idempotent_write"] — each capability influences how the SDK retries and what it exposes to callers.
ryan: example mapping?
nina: sure: if transport advertises progressive_stream -> SDK prefers streaming Readable/AsyncIterator (emit partials). if server_cursor -> SDK exposes .resume_cursor; if stateless_resume -> server gives opaque token we can store client-side.
lee: what about transports that only support fetch-style pages (no streaming/no resume)? fallback should be page-level fetch with conservative retry. keep simple for browser consumers.
omar: token shape question: earlier discussion suggested JSON then base64. i worry about token size and evolution. propose: token_v1 = base64url(cbor({v:1, cursor, meta_checksum})) — compact, versioned.
ryan: CBOR makes sense for compactness. cross-lang CBOR libs exist but adds dependency. alternative: short opaque ID (server lookup) for most flows, and full-state token only behind advanced capability flag.
nina: yep — default: opaque server handle (best practice). only when transport advertises stateless_resume do we accept and roundtrip client-provided state. docs must strongly warn about storing full state.
lee: retry granularity nuances: per-item retry vs per-page vs per-stream-resume. I think default behavior should be: 1) for reads, retry at page/resume-token granularity; 2) for streaming partials, emit what we have and persist last-good token; 3) for mutating streams use idempotency-key per operation.
omar: agree. edge case: long-running stream that yields many items and connection drops mid-item. how do we convey partial progress?
ryan: add optional progress markers in items: {type: 'progress', seq: 123, partial: true}. SDK exposes a hook to the application: onPartial(item, resume_token). opt-in in request options.
nina: cross-language surface: TS -> AsyncIterable<Item> with helper obj: iterator.getResume() or iterator.resume(); Python -> async generator with attribute .resume_token on the generator object; Go -> Iterator struct with ResumeToken() string and Persist() helper. keep naming consistent: ResumeToken, ResumeCursor, ResumeHandle — pick "resume_token" in wire and map to idiomatic names per language.
lee: sample TS pseudocode:```ts
const it = client.listRecords({limit: 50, hints: ['server_cursor']});
for await (const page of it) {
  // page.items
  const tok = it.getResume();
}
```
ryan: Python sketch:```py
ait = client.list_records(limit=50, hints=['server_cursor'])
async for page in ait:
    # page.items
# later
if getattr(ait, 'resume_token', None):
    store(ait.resume_token)
```
lee: Go sketch:```go
it := client.ListRecords(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() {
  rec := it.Item()
}
if t := it.ResumeToken(); t != "" {
  save(t)
}
```
omar: testing and CI: need contract tests for capability negotiation, token roundtrip, token-version-mismatch handling, and behavior when token invalidated (expired/model-change).
ci-bot: CI plan created: sdk-paging-cap-contract matrix with permutations: fetch-only, streaming+cursor, streaming+stateless_resume, mock-invalid-token. Jobs added for ts, py, go runners.
ryan: error handling UX: when resume token checksum mismatch return typed error ResumeIncompatibleError with guidance "invalidate local token and retry from scratch". avoid silent fallbacks.
nina: security note: tokens must never contain prompt text or sensitive fields. server must redact. SDK should validate token length and reject obviously huge tokens unless user explicitly opts-in.
lee: migration concerns: existing SDKs that always returned full response bodies may need minor shim to expose iterator resume metadata. propose opt-in flag in v2: {expose_resume: true} and default to false for backward compat.
omar: telemetry: emit metrics when we fall back to non-resumable behavior, token failures, and number of retries saved by resume. helps quantify value.
ci-bot: added telemetry hooks to sdk-metrics lib + test harness. will gate telemetry on env var during tests. :robot_face:
ryan: operational note: runtime (server) needs to advertise capability headers early (e.g., X-RW-Capabilities: streaming,server_cursor,stateless_resume). SDK caches capability per-host for short TTL to avoid per-request negotiation cost.
nina: agreed. also include a small negotiation handshake in the protocol so SDK can request minimal set and server responds with supported subset. keep handshake lightweight (single header roundtrip).
lee: docs: cookbooks for "fast streaming" vs "durable resume" patterns. include code examples and pitfalls (token leakage, model-rolling invalidations).
omar: ok next steps: nina drafts a short RFC + example snippets for ts/py/go, ryan will add contract tests in harness, lee will author cookbook doc.
nina: thanks — i'll post the RFC in #eng-platform by EOD tomorrow. feedback welcome. :wave:
